newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile shares end weaker on inflation forecast.
newsitem.headline: Chile shares end weaker on inflation forecast.

text.p: Chilean shares closed lower with the bolsa hurt by Wall Street's weakness and higher than-expected inflation forecasts for February, said traders.

Stocks are seen angling lower again at the opening on fears that a surge in inflation in February will delay a further cut in interest rates by the Central Bank, said Jaime Pena y Lillo, portfolio manager at brokerage Socimer.
"The inflation signal surprised many people and they now doubt whether the authorities can relax their monetary policy," said Pena y Lillo.
The IPSA index ended down 0.38 percent at 115.42 points.
The general IGPA index lost 0.22 percent to 5,346.31 points amid turnover of 11.8 billion pesos.
The bolsa slipped at the opening on the Central Bank's forecast that consumer prices will rise 0.6 percent this month, against analysts' estimates of 0.4-0.5 percent, said dealers.
Consumer prices rose 0.5 percent in February last year.
Investors had been expecting the Bank to clip rates again next month but these hopes have been dampened after the lastest inflation data, said dealers.

Losers included electricity shares with prices adjusting as the stocks have been overvalued recently taking into the account the serious impact of this year's drought on companies' earnings, they said.
Endesa lost 0.99 percent to 251 pesos, while Enersis ENI.Nu shed 0.56 percent to 267-1/2 pesos.
Winners included telecom Telex which climbed 5.94 percent to 1,160 pesos on foreign demand.
Brokers said they did not know any reason for the stock's surge.
